thinking_and_logic: The solution maintains a hash map from number to its index for elements already processed. For each number n at index i, it computes complement = target - n and checks if that complement has been seen; if so, it returns the stored index and i. Checking before inserting ensures the same element is not used twice, and the single pass guarantees O(n) expected time.
code_assessment: Your final code essentially matches the answer key’s optimal approach: single pass + hash map, complement check before insertion. This avoids known pitfalls like sorting (which loses original indices) and accidentally reusing the same element. The only minor improvement area is how to handle the “no solution” path in a more general setting (exception or None), but given the guarantee, returning [] is fine for the prompt.
